inlines.v: CONTINUAL, adjective [Latin See Continue.] 1. Proceeding without interruption or cessation; unceasing; not intermitting; used in reference to time. He that hath a merry heart hath a continual feast. Proverbs 15:15. I have great heaviness and continual sorrow of heart. Romans 9:2. 2. Very frequent; often repeated; as, the charitable man has continual application for alms. 3. continual fever, or continued fever, a fever that abates, but never entirely intermits, till it comes to a crisis; thus distinguished from remitting and intermitting fever. 4. continual claim, in law, a claim that is made from time to time within every year or day, to land or other estate, the possession of which cannot be obtained without hazard. 5. Perpetual.
